notes: I re-derived the solution: velocity is one over two a x plus b, its derivative with distance is minus two a v squared, and multiplying by v gives the third option. mistakes[0] 'concept' is right: calling the derivative of velocity with distance the acceleration is a wrong belief about what acceleration is, not an algebra slip, and the solution's own hint agrees. Its route says that and nothing else, in first person, with no digits. right_route names the move that separates the right method from that belief (multiply by the velocity). It is a later step than step one, but it is the approach's defining move and the sidecar follows that convention across this slice, so I did not file it; the pair is clearly tellable apart on the menu.
